title: Wear on Quay Street: stains, grime, gum, cracked render and the street's other marks
summary_line: 23 kinds of seeded greyscale wear mask, each with its rule of place, size and shape in metres, density, tone per surface, wet and dry look, texel scale and checks, from 20 measurements on CC0 photographs and the Hook sheet; real road and pavement wear is low-contrast and broad, wall feet and streaks follow the Hook sheet's heavier mood, and nothing from 2000s Britain or America is in it.

units.tone: sRGB 0-255, albedo multiplier in linear light, L* is CIE D65

scene.street: Quay Street, the Hook, Meridian; 48 m, 6.0 m carriageway (two 3.0 m lanes, crossfall 1:40, crown 75 mm above the channel), footways 2.0 m (1:40), kerb upstand 0.125, channel course 0.255 wide
scene.east_side: six-bay Victorian shop parade, 6 m bays, faces WEST (the wet side in the UK's prevailing south-westerly)
scene.west_side: shop block (north half) and plain terraces (quay end), faces EAST

layers.L1: rule-placed wall decals from the kinds with layer L1: yaw-faced, normal-faded (PAINTED-FRONTS-2026-10-07 section 1)
layers.L2: ground marks written once into the ground's virtual texture
layers.L3: a few hand-placed hero decals at the near frontages (the pale patch on the left gable; Mickey's wall foot)
layers.mask_encoding: 8-bit greyscale PNG, 0 = nothing, 255 = the kind's full effect; decals are rectangular crops; stamps have a 4 texel clear border; hard-edged kinds (paint_flake, render_crack) are near-binary; builder colours by surface from 'tone'; strength = house wear x mask

streak_sill.label: Rain streaks under window sills

where.feature: the lower edge of every window sill, upper floors and shop transom ledges alike; one set per sill
where.rule: Origin on the sill's lower edge. Two end streaks start under the sill's two ends (where the sill sheds its water); 3 to 7 thin rivulets start at brackets, joints and chips along the sill; a faint wash spans the sill. Everything runs straight down (gravity), tilted at most 3 degrees. Never rotate a streak.
where.height_m: 0 to 1.6 below the sill's lower edge; stop at the next ledge, string course or door head if nearer
where.sides: East parade fronts face west, the wet side of a British port: weight 1.0. West block fronts face east: weight 0.7. Gable ends facing the street: 0.8.
where.footfall_and_wet: Not footfall. Wet climate: always present; darker and glossier when wet; the lower half dries first.

era_rules: Heavy: 1990 walls were sootier and 1990 pavements dirtier than any modern panorama measured (the 2019 London photographs are the cleanest end of the range). Where a photograph and the Hook sheet disagree, the target sits between them, nearer the sheet for walls (the sheet is the mood bar) and nearer the photograph for ground marks.

Nothing later than 1990, or unusual in an old quarter then (Judgement on each): no tactile or blister paving, red or green anti-skid surfacing, thermoplastic bus lanes, pressure-washed stripes, bike-lane green, spray utility markings, cycle stands, wheelie-bin lines, vape and mask litter, QR-code stickers, anti-bird spikes, uPVC white fronts.

No American marks: no wide white parking T-markings, no painted crosswalk zebras in white 12-inch bars, no manhole lids with US castings, no fire-hydrant paint, no yellow centre-line pairs, no graffiti throw-ups in bubble-letter style (the street's graffiti are the canon's five tags, in another family).
No alcohol or gambling traces: no bottles, cans, bar-mats, betting slips or scratch cards in the litter (canon content rule). Tobacco ends are allowed.

M01.label: Dry asphalt albedo on eight scans
M01.method: Central 70 % of each 2k diffuse map; per-channel median; L* from sRGB D65.
M01.error: +/-3 sRGB levels (JPEG, unknown colour cast of each scan); scans are de-lit albedo.
M01.reading: Worn dry asphalt spans L* 25 to 59, median of the mid scans (asphalt_02, aerial_asphalt_01, asphalt_01) 91/86/82, L* 37.

M02.label: Wear marks on a 30 m x 30 m worn road scan (aerial_asphalt_01)
M02.method: L* smoothed 44 mm (removes the aggregate), minus L* smoothed 0.88 m; dark marks = deficit beyond a threshold; connected components; linear = aspect > 6 and length > 0.5 m; cross-profile averaged about the skeleton of the 16 linear marks.
M02.error: Thresholds +/-1 L*: share 4.6 % (dL 4) to 23.5 % (dL 1.5). Widths +/-15 mm (7 mm pixel). The tile is a tileable processed scan: spacing of features is the photographer's tile, not a street.
M02.reading: Real road wear is low contrast and broad: 4 to 12 % of the area is marked, blobs about 0.22 m, tyre scuffs about 90 mm wide and 2 to 8 m long, with soft edges about 70 mm.

M03.label: Cracks in a worn asphalt scan (asphalt_02, 3 m x 3 m)
M03.method: Counted by eye on the 1400 px montage with a 3.0 m scale (automatic ridge detection failed on the aggregate and was abandoned): one sealed crack the full 3.0 m, six hairlines 0.2 to 1.8 m, total about 7.3 m.
M03.error: +/-30 % on length; the patch was chosen by its photographer as a cracked road, so it is the worst case.
M03.reading: A cracked road carries 0.8 m of crack per m2; typical road 0.1 to 0.4 (Judgement).

M04.label: Oil drip speckle on asphalt in a London residential street (urban_street_03, 8k panorama, ground ortho-rectified)
M04.method: Panorama re-projected to a top-down ortho tile at 3 mm/px with camera height 1.6 m; scale proved by the yellow kerb line: 24 to 26 px = 72 to 78 mm (line is 75 mm). Dots = pixels darker than 0.85, 0.75, 0.65 of a 25 px median; components of 4 px or more.
M04.error: Height 1.6 +/-0.1 m gives +/-6 % on areas and +/-6 % on lengths; dot sizes +/-2 mm (3 mm pixel); threshold changes density by a factor 2.5 (167 to 67 per m2).

values.note_region: per_m2_* are over the whole 1.33 m2 region of the view, which includes clean asphalt around the dotted band; in_band_* divide by the band's own area (length x width, central 90 % of the dots)

M04.reading: A parked car's drip band: about 0.3 m x 1.8 m (at least), dots 17 mm, 0.7 of the road's luminance, 154 per m2 inside the band at the darker threshold (379 at the lighter).

M05.label: Utility reinstatement in asphalt (urban_street_02, ortho tile)
M05.method: Ortho tile 3 mm/px, h 1.6 m: rectangle spans 370 x 360 px; seam darker band 10 to 17 px; grass tufts at 3 corners.
M05.error: +/-0.1 m on size (height), +/-10 mm on seam.
M05.reading: A cover reinstatement is about 1.0 x 1.1 m with a dark seam of 30 to 50 mm.

M06.label: Litter along the kerb and on the road (urban_street_02, rectilinear view yaw -165, pitch -20)
M06.method: Pieces counted by eye on a marked picture (automatic bright-blob detection also hit aggregate glints and was rejected): kerb strip about 22 pieces over 5 m of kerb, band 0.3 m deep; road 10 pieces over 13.6 m2. Detected bright bits (aggregate included) had size 7.6, 11.2, 27.7 mm at p10/50/90.
M06.error: +/-35 % on counts; 8k pixel at 7 m is 5 mm.
M06.reading: The kerb gathers about 4 pieces per metre; open road about 0.7 per m2 (a scruffier estate road; a 1990 shop street would be at or above this).

M07.label: Patched flags (urban_street_03, ortho tile of the footway, camera-to-footway 1.48 m)
M07.method: Six slab samples by rectangle, mean linear luminance and sRGB; dark slabs 0.20 to 0.24, pale 0.34 to 0.42 (same light); shares and cracks by eye over about 18 slabs.
M07.error: Luminance ratio +/-0.08; shares +/-10 points; slab size +/-15 % (height of the footway).
M07.reading: A 1990-style patched footway has a 0.58 luminance ratio between old and replacement flags and about 1 flag in 9 cracked.

preview_boxes.format: [x0, x1, y0, y1] in preview pixels

M08.label: Flaking paint (peeling_painted_wall, 1.8 m, 0.88 mm/px)
M08.method: Lab k-means (k=2, five seeds) on 512 px, nearest-centroid on 1024 px; minority cluster = loss; components of 3 px or more; edge width = 0.8 x contrast / median boundary gradient.
M08.error: Share +/-2 points; sizes +/-1 mm (1.76 mm px at 1024); edge width limited by one pixel (0.4 mm means 'hard edge').
M08.reading: Flakes are small (17 mm), many (38 per m2), aspect about 3, with hard edges.

M09.label: Craquelure in old paint/render (preconcrete_wall_001, 4 m; cracked_concrete_wall, 1 m)
M09.method: Dark-line detection (L below 10 px local mean by 6 to 8 L*), elongated components >= 40 mm, Zhang-Suen skeleton length; cell size and flake size by eye on the montage.
M09.error: Length +/-30 % (blur merges and splits); width includes blur (true hairline 3 to 8 mm).
M09.reading: Map cracking runs 4 to 6 m per m2 of affected render in cells 0.14 to 0.23 m.

M10.label: Large paint/render loss (rebar_reinforced_concrete, 2 m)
M10.method: As M08, k=3; exposed clusters 0 and 2.
M10.reading: A neglected painted wall can lose up to 40 % of its paint in patches 0.1 to 0.3 m with edges about 10 mm soft.

M11.label: Render loss revealing brick (damaged_plaster, 1.85 m)
M11.method: As M08, k=3; exposed brick = cluster 1.
M11.reading: Render loss: 18 % of the area, patches 67 mm median, up to 0.45 m, edges 11 mm.

M12.label: Damp and mould blotches on painted render (concrete_wall_003, 3 m)
M12.method: As M08, k=3; cluster 2 = dark blotch, clusters 0+2 = yellow stain and blotch.
M12.reading: Damp blotches: 12 % of the wall, median 42 mm, p90 171 mm, 19 mm soft edge; cream render goes to 144/124/97 (x0.45 on Y).

M13.label: Dark corrosion streaks (rusty_painted_metal, 2.2 m)
M13.method: As M08, k=3, cluster 1 = dark streaks.
M13.error: +/-4 points; metal not masonry: geometry only.
M13.reading: Run-off streaks: 24 mm wide (p50), aspect 4 to 12, edges 16 mm.

M14.label: Rust trickle from a fixing and rust drops (asbestos_sheet_02, 1.8 m)
M14.method: Rust = (R - B) > 45 and R > 90 on a crop; trickle rows and widths read from the mask; also by eye.
M14.reading: A rust trickle is 5 to 20 mm wide and at least 0.5 m long, with drops 30 to 90 mm at its end.

M15.label: Moss in joints and the algae gradient at a plastered wall foot
M15.method: As M08 for moss (green cluster); for plaster_brick_01 the row profile of green excess (G - mean(R,B)) and L*, rows 1024 to 2048 are the plaster (lower 1.35 m).
M15.reading: Moss fills 12 to 17 % of a wet brick wall as joint lines; on render the lowest 0.45 m goes olive-green and 20 L* darker.

M16.label: Drip streaks hanging from a horizontal joint (concrete_layers, 1.55 m, 0.757 mm/px)
M16.method: L* minus its 12 px mean < -1.5 / -2.5; vertical opening (3 x 1); components with height >= 4 x width and >= 60 mm.
M16.error: Counts +/-40 % (stronger streaks only; by eye 10 to 15 per metre); widths +/-2 mm.
M16.reading: Individual rivulets are 10 to 20 mm wide, 0.09 to 0.45 m long, 8 to 15 per metre of joint, both dark and lime-pale.

M17.label: Streak under a sill bracket on yellow stock brick (urban_street_03, yaw 105, bay window)
M17.method: Scale from brick courses (75 mm gauge, 30 px at 2x crop); column under the central bracket 40 px wide, 180 px long; mean luminance of the column against flanks 0.97; darkest bricks 0.80 to 0.90.
M17.reading: On a maintained 2019 London brick wall the sill-bracket streak is faint: 0.10 m x 0.45 m, 3 to 20 % darker. The Hook sheet bar is heavier; the target sits between.

M18.label: Hook sheet, left gable foot (mood bar, not a photograph)
M18.method: Column-median luminance profile of columns 15 to 170, rows 380 to 730; brick course from autocorrelation (11 px = 75 mm, so 6.8 mm/px); wall reference rows 430 to 600.
M18.reading: The sheet's foot: 0.33 m black band (0.12 to 0.30 of the wall), a 0.15 to 0.22 m grey-white band on its upper flank (0.26 to 0.46 m), a ragged top stepping by courses.

M19.label: Hook sheet, pale patch on the left gable
M19.method: Patch size from courses: 3.8 courses high, about 1.3 brick lengths wide; colour mean of its core.
M19.reading: A buff mortar patch 0.3 m square, 34 L* lighter than the wall.

M20.label: Hook sheet, right pavement stains and road blots
M20.method: Colour of one brown stain 85/60/44 against flag 136/129/131; sizes relative to a 0.6 m flag by eye.
M20.error: +/-30 % size; 5 per 10 m2 by counting 7 stains over about 14 m2.
M20.reading: The mood bar's pavement carries brown stains 27 L* darker than the flags, 0.15 to 0.45 m, about 5 per 10 m2.
